top_choice_rationale: The magic-wavelength optical lattice clock is an original invention, a distinct principle from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes, and it is experimentally verified by several independent laboratories reaching about 10^-18 and comparing clocks across sites. It opens a door to millimetre-scale gravitational redshift, bounds on varying constants and dark-matter couplings. The two-name credit (Katori for the proposal and first realisation, Ye for the route to 10^-18) is consistent with the record, provided the citation names the lattice concept and not optical clocks or precision in general. No award is the only alternative on this slate and is clearly weaker.
